advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify or derive `_CAP_MANIFESTS` rather than hardcoding it, and document why a second curated list here does not reintroduce the drift class the gate exists to prevent.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:12: `This gate does NOT introduce a second curated "deploy-relevant files" list (that just` / `relocates the drift).`
The tuple encodes a design invariant (caps consumed by both re-materialization surfaces) that is not derived from any source autodeploy maintains for its own reasons.
advisory.finding: `_CAP_MANIFESTS = ("MATERIALIZER_PATHS", "OBS_PATHS")` hardcodes, inside the checker, WHICH consuming manifests each cap script must appear in. This is a second hand-curated list of exactly the kind the module docstring says the gate must NOT introduce ("This gate does NOT introduce a second curated 'deploy-relevant files' list (that just relocates the drift)"). If autodeploy's consuming design changes (a manifest is renamed, or a cap should be consumed by a third manifest), this tuple silently drifts and no derivation catches it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] De-duplicate cap diagnostics so a cap absent from all manifests is not reported by both the union check and every per-manifest check.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:270-274: union `uncovered` diagnostic `UNCOVERED {path} ... listed in NO autodeploy.sh *_PATHS manifest`
scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:275-279: `_cap_manifest_gaps` diagnostic `UNCOVERED {path} ... listed in NO {manifest} consuming manifest`
A cap in no manifest fails `is_covered(path, tokens)` (union) AND `is_covered(path, manifests.get(manifest))` for both entries of `_CAP_MANIFESTS`, yielding 1 + 2 diagnostics.
advisory.finding: A cap script that is absent from EVERY manifest is reported multiple times: once by the union-based `uncovered(...)` loop and once per manifest by `_cap_manifest_gaps(...)` (i.e. up to three diagnostics for one path). The two diagnostics also use near-identical wording ("listed in NO ... manifest"), making the operator output redundant and potentially confusing about whether these are distinct failures.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a direct unit test for `parse_manifest_paths_by_name` asserting tokens are segregated per manifest name (e.g. `A_PATHS='x'\nB_PATHS='y'` yields `{'A_PATHS': {'x'}, 'B_PATHS': {'y'}}` and no cross-leak).
evidence: ABSENCE: `search_files` for `parse_manifest_paths_by_name` in tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py returned `(no matches)` — the union variant `parse_manifest_paths` has direct tests (test_parse_manifest_paths_unions_all_paths_blocks, test_parse_manifest_paths_ignores_trailing_inline_comments) but the by-name variant does not.

The `tokens = set()` reset per line at scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:111 is the segregation logic; a regression that failed to reset would leak tokens across manifest names, silently defeating the 'require in BOTH manifests' contract without a direct test to catch it.
advisory.finding: The new `parse_manifest_paths_by_name` — the function that keys path tokens per `*_PATHS` manifest name and underpins the whole per-manifest cap gate — has no direct unit test. Its by-name segregation (ensuring MATERIALIZER_PATHS tokens do not leak into OBS_PATHS's set, and vice versa) is only exercised indirectly through the end-to-end RED cap test.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Parametrize `test_red_when_a_cap_script_is_omitted_from_a_consuming_manifest` over `_CAP_SCRIPTS` as well as manifest name so every derived cap script's omission is exercised.
evidence: tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py:98-99 shows the pattern for thorough coverage: `@pytest.mark.parametrize("target", _COVERED_DERIVED)` drives every covered path individually.
`_CAP_SCRIPTS` (test lines 33-38) enumerates all four cap scripts, but only one is mutated in the RED consuming-manifest test.
advisory.finding: The RED cap-omission test exercises only `infra/scripts/docker-storage-cap.sh`; the other three derived cap scripts (container-cap.sh, journald-cap.sh, vartmp-cap.sh) are never driven through the consuming-manifest omission path, unlike the sibling covered-path mutation test which is parametrized across every covered path.
